description: Make the native libretro loader (crates/emulator-bridge/src/cores/native_core.rs) able to boot a real PS1 core (PCSX ReARMed) through the SOFTWARE frame path, as a thin passthrough (dlopen + forward retro_*). Today on_environment answers only ~6 commands and video() hardcodes PixelFormat::Rgba8888. PCSX ReARMed will not boot against that: it calls SET_PIXEL_FORMAT (10) inside retro_load_game (choosing RGB565 by default or XRGB8888 if the pcsx_rearmed_rgb32_output option is on), issues 73 GET_VARIABLE (15) reads, and declares need_fullpath=true - hard-rejecting load if info->path is NULL. This feature closes those gaps in Rust only. It must keep the switch-stub working (15/15 harness) and the 74 cargo tests green. All work stays behind the existing native-core feature gate; the wasm build must be untouched.
steps: In native_core.rs, extend the on_environment C callback to answer the commands PCSX ReARMed needs for a first boot. MANDATORY: SET_PIXEL_FORMAT (10) - read the *const c_uint the core points at, map it via crate::frame::PixelFormat::from_libretro (libretro 1=XRGB8888, 2=RGB565; reject 0=0RGB1555 by returning false), store the chosen format so video() can report it, and return true; GET_VARIABLE (15) - the data is a *mut retro_variable {key: *const c_char, value: *mut *const c_char}; set value to null (or leave it) and return false, which libretro defines as 'use the core default' (do NOT fabricate option strings). ACCEPT-AND-NOOP (return true, take no action): SET_VARIABLES (16), SET_CORE_OPTIONS (52), SET_CORE_OPTIONS_INTL (53), SET_CORE_OPTIONS_V2 (67), SET_CORE_OPTIONS_V2_INTL (68), SET_CORE_OPTIONS_DISPLAY, SET_CORE_OPTIONS_UPDATE_DISPLAY_CALLBACK, SET_INPUT_DESCRIPTORS (11), SET_CONTROLLER_INFO (35), SET_PERFORMANCE_LEVEL (8), SET_SYSTEM_AV_INFO (32), SET_GEOMETRY (37), SET_MESSAGE (6), SET_MESSAGE_EXT, SET_SUPPORT_NO_GAME (already handled), SET_MINIMUM_AUDIO_LATENCY, SET_AUDIO_BUFFER_STATUS_CALLBACK (accept but store nothing - do NOT claim support then never call back; if unsure, return false to refuse cleanly, mirroring the web build's documented lesson in SESSION_HANDOFF §1). GET_VARIABLE_UPDATE (17) already returns false=no-change. GET_CAN_DUPE (3) already true. GET_SYSTEM_DIRECTORY (9)/GET_SAVE_DIRECTORY (31) already implemented. Keep GET_INPUT_BITMASKS unhandled (return false) so the core falls back to per-id input_state, which InputSnapshot::libretro_state already serves. Refuse everything else by returning false (no logging on the default arm to avoid per-frame log spam, matching the existing style).

Machine-check every environment command number against .work/hdr/libretro/libretro.h before writing it (SESSION_HANDOFF §1 documents that experimental-bit mistakes produce a case that can never match). Add a brief comment next to each constant citing its libretro.h value.

Add a stored negotiated-pixel-format field to NativeLibretroCore (e.g. `negotiated_format: PixelFormat`), defaulting to the descriptor's declared pixel_format. Because on_environment is a bare C fn with no self, route the negotiated format through a mechanism consistent with the existing design: either a process-global Mutex<Option<PixelFormat>> alongside DIRECTORIES (written by SET_PIXEL_FORMAT during retro_load_game, read back into the struct right after load_content's load_game call), or the EXCHANGE thread-local if load_content runs on the same thread as the callback. Prefer the DIRECTORIES-style global for the same lifetime reason documented for DIRECTORIES (load happens under a Mutex-held bridge, possibly off the callback thread). Reset it before each load so a stale value from a prior core cannot leak.

Change video() to report the negotiated format instead of the hardcoded PixelFormat::Rgba8888. RGB565 and XRGB8888 are both normalised on the CPU side by gfx/convert.rs, so reporting the true format is what makes PS1 colours correct. Keep the last_was_hardware / empty-pixels early return unchanged.

Confirm load_content passes a real openable fullpath. PCSX ReARMed requires info->path != NULL (frontend/libretro.c ~2010 'info->path required') and reads the file itself; it ignores the data pointer for disc content. The current code sets info.path from CString::new(hint.name) - hint.name is the file *stem* with no directory, which is NOT an openable path. Adjust so that when content bytes are empty (the need_fullpath case), the path handed to retro_load_game is the full filesystem path the caller provided. Determine the cleanest seam: ContentHint currently carries only extension+name. Either (a) add an optional full_path to ContentHint and populate it from the launch path, or (b) document that for need_fullpath native cores the caller passes the absolute path as the content 'name'/filename and load_content uses it verbatim. Choose the option that keeps the web build and the switch-stub path unchanged, and wire launch() in uniffi_api.rs accordingly if ContentHint changes. Do not break the stub, which passes a real temp path already.

If ContentHint or any signature changes, update all call sites (bridge.rs launch, uniffi_api.rs launch which calls ContentHint::from_filename, wasm.rs if shared, and the switch-stub's expectations) and keep from_filename behaviour identical for the web build.

Add or extend unit tests in native_core.rs (behind #[cfg(all(not(target_arch="wasm32"), feature="native-core"))] and #[cfg(test)]) that exercise the new logic WITHOUT a real dylib: e.g. a test that drives on_environment with SET_PIXEL_FORMAT for RGB565 and XRGB8888 and asserts the stored format matches, a test that SET_PIXEL_FORMAT with 0RGB1555 (libretro 0) is refused (returns false), and a test that GET_VARIABLE returns false and leaves value null. If on_environment is not directly testable due to the global, factor the command-handling into a small pure helper (cmd, and a safe representation of the payload) that both the extern C fn and the tests call, so the mapping is unit-tested. These tests must run under plain `cargo test`.
Run the full local verification suite and confirm no regressions.
acceptance_criteria: native_core.rs on_environment answers SET_PIXEL_FORMAT (10) by storing the core-chosen format and returning true for RGB565/XRGB8888, and false for 0RGB1555.

native_core.rs on_environment answers GET_VARIABLE (15) by returning false with a null value (core uses defaults), and accepts the SET_VARIABLES/SET_CORE_OPTIONS* / input-descriptor / geometry / message families as no-ops returning true.
video() returns FrameView whose format is the negotiated format, not a hardcoded value; defaults to the declared descriptor format when no SET_PIXEL_FORMAT arrived.
load_content passes a real openable filesystem path to retro_load_game for need_fullpath content, so a core that hard-requires info->path can load; the switch-stub path still works.
New unit tests covering pixel-format negotiation (accept 565/XRGB8888, reject 0RGB1555) and GET_VARIABLE default behaviour pass under `cargo test`.
cargo test still reports all tests passing (>= 74 + the new ones).
cargo check for aarch64-apple-ios (both default and --profile ios) and clippy (native-core,uniffi-bindings, --all-targets) are clean.
The wasm/web build code paths are untouched (no new deps, no changes gated outside cfg(not wasm32)+native-core, from_filename behaviour identical).
findings:
Implemented FEAT-002 entirely in Rust, all behind the existing native-core gate; the wasm/web build is untouched (verified with `cargo check --target wasm32-unknown-unknown`).

native_core.rs:
- Rewrote on_environment. Every command constant was machine-checked against .work/hdr/libretro/libretro.h and carries an inline comment citing its header line. IMPORTANT CORRECTION vs the prose in this feature: the prose listed 'SET_CORE_OPTIONS (52)' and 'SET_CORE_OPTIONS_INTL (53)', but the header says 52=GET_CORE_OPTIONS_VERSION, 53=SET_CORE_OPTIONS, 54=SET_CORE_OPTIONS_INTL, 55=SET_CORE_OPTIONS_DISPLAY, 60=SET_MESSAGE_EXT, 62=SET_AUDIO_BUFFER_STATUS_CALLBACK, 63=SET_MINIMUM_AUDIO_LATENCY, 67=SET_CORE_OPTIONS_V2, 68=SET_CORE_OPTIONS_V2_INTL, 69=SET_CORE_OPTIONS_UPDATE_DISPLAY_CALLBACK. I used the header values (the step explicitly instructs machine-checking against libretro.h). GET_CORE_OPTIONS_VERSION(52) now returns 0 (honest: we implement the SET_CORE_OPTIONS* no-op surface but none of the query surface, keeping the core on the SET_VARIABLES-era path).
- SET_PIXEL_FORMAT(10): reads the *const c_uint, maps via PixelFormat::from_libretro (1=XRGB8888, 2=RGB565), stores the chosen format and returns true; refuses 0RGB1555 (returns false, stores nothing).
- GET_VARIABLE(15): nulls the retro_variable.value slot and returns false (core uses its defaults); does NOT fabricate option strings.
- Accept-and-noop (return true): SET_SUPPORT_NO_GAME, SET_CONTENT_INFO_OVERRIDE, SET_VARIABLES, all SET_CORE_OPTIONS* variants + DISPLAY + UPDATE_DISPLAY_CALLBACK, SET_INPUT_DESCRIPTORS, SET_CONTROLLER_INFO, SET_PERFORMANCE_LEVEL, SET_SYSTEM_AV_INFO, SET_GEOMETRY, SET_MESSAGE, SET_MESSAGE_EXT, SET_MINIMUM_AUDIO_LATENCY. Kept GET_CAN_DUPE(3)=true and GET_VARIABLE_UPDATE(17)=false. Deliberately NOT accepted: SET_AUDIO_BUFFER_STATUS_CALLBACK(62) and GET_INPUT_BITMASKS(51|EXPERIMENTAL) both fall through to the silent default false arm, per SESSION_HANDOFF §1 (never claim a callback we won't make; refusing bitmasks routes the core to per-id input_state which InputSnapshot::libretro_state serves). Default arm stays silent (no per-frame log spam).
- Pixel-format storage: added a process-global NEGOTIATED_FORMAT: Mutex<Option<PixelFormat>> alongside DIRECTORIES (same lifetime rationale: SET_PIXEL_FORMAT fires inside retro_load_game under a Mutex-held bridge, possibly off the callback thread). Helpers reset_negotiated_format / store_negotiated_format / take_negotiated_format. Added negotiated_format: PixelFormat to NativeLibretroCore, seeded from descriptor.pixel_format. load_content resets the global before load_game and reads it back after, updating the field. video() now reports self.negotiated_format instead of the hardcoded PixelFormat::Rgba8888; the last_was_hardware/empty-pixels early return is unchanged.
- Fullpath: load_content now hands retro_load_game the caller's real full path when content bytes are empty (the need_fullpath case), falling back to hint.name otherwise. This fixes PCSX ReARMed's hard requirement that info->path be a real openable path (hint.name is only the file stem).

cores/mod.rs:
- Added ContentHint.full_path: Option<String> (default None). ContentHint::from_filename now retains the verbatim string in full_path only when the input contains a '/' (i.e. it is a path); extension/name splitting is byte-for-byte identical, so the web build and the switch-stub behaviour are unchanged. No call-site signature changes were needed (uniffi_api.rs launch already passes the filename through from_filename; the Swift side passes the absolute path as the filename, per the existing uniffi_api comment).

Tests (native_core.rs, #[cfg(test)], run under `cargo test --features native-core`): SET_PIXEL_FORMAT stores RGB565 and XRGB8888; 0RGB1555 refused with nothing stored; GET_VARIABLE returns false and nulls value; GET_VARIABLE_UPDATE reports no-change; the option/message families accepted as no-ops; SET_AUDIO_BUFFER_STATUS_CALLBACK(62) refused; GET_INPUT_BITMASKS refused; GET_CORE_OPTIONS_VERSION reports 0; from_filename records full_path only for paths. A dedicated FORMAT_TEST_LOCK serialises the tests that touch the global. Note: the native_core module is feature-gated, so these tests compile/run under `cargo test --features native-core` (10 new -> 84 total); plain `cargo test` stays at 74 because the module is not compiled without the feature (matches the step's own gating instruction).

Verification (all green): cargo test (74) and cargo test --features native-core,uniffi-bindings (84); cargo check --target aarch64-apple-ios --features native-core,uniffi-bindings; cargo check --profile ios --target aarch64-apple-ios --features native-core,uniffi-bindings; cargo clippy --features native-core,uniffi-bindings --all-targets -- -D warnings (clean); ./native/switch-wrapper/build.sh host (15/15); cargo check --target wasm32-unknown-unknown (web build untouched).
